title: He held the world in his hands…
paragraphs:
He held the world in his hands…
but his soul was slipping through his fingers.
You can feel it, can’t you?

That quiet tension nobody posts about.
That inner war behind the wins.
That strange emptiness that shows up… right after success.

You prayed for more.
You worked for more.
You chased more.
Why does your soul feel… less?
Here’s the question nobody wants to answer:

What if the life you’re building…
is costing you the life God gave you?

What if the applause is loud…
but heaven is silent?
Because this isn’t just about money.
It’s about the slow, almost invisible drift where:

You stop praying like you used to.
You justify what once convicted you.
You normalize what once broke your heart.
Until your soul becomes a stranger to the presence of God.
“For what will it profit a man if he gains the whole world and loses his own soul?” — Mark 8:36

Not your job.
Not your reputation.
Not your relationships.
The word Jesus uses for “soul” points to your very life—your eternal self, your identity before God.
This is not about temporary loss.

You can win here…
and lose forever.
Some scholars interpret this passage as a direct confrontation against self-centered ambition—where a person elevates success, power, or comfort above obedience to God.
Others emphasize the eternal weight of the soul—reminding us that no earthly gain can compensate for spiritual ruin.
Either way, the message is clear:
There is no trade worth your soul.
But here’s where it gets even more personal.
Because this isn’t just about obvious sin.
The kind you’ve learned to manage.
The kind you’ve hidden so well… even you don’t call it sin anymore.
Because the same Jesus who asked that question…
walked toward a cross with your name on His heart.
“But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
While you were slowly trading your soul—
Your sin was not ignored—it was judged.
Your shame was not dismissed—it was carried.
Your debt was not minimized—it was paid in full.
Because Jesus doesn’t just warn you about losing your soul…
“For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.” — Luke 19:10
that is slowly letting go of God?
that is quietly costing you your soul?
Jesus already told us the way back:
“Whoever wants to be my disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me.” — Mark 8:34

The pride.
The secret sin.
The control.
Because eternity is not a theory.
And every step you take is leading somewhere.
If this is hitting you deep…
